# karpo-apple-silicon

> Unofficial community port that runs MachinePulse's Karpo Decision models (karpo-decision-31B and karpo-decision-12B, the Gemma 4 family checkpoints) on Apple Silicon Macs. One small PyTorch patch for the MPS (Metal) GPU, plus an experimental MLX path with 8-bit and 4-bit quantized weights. Apache-2.0. Not affiliated with MachinePulse or Google.

## The short answer

Karpo Decision as published needs an NVIDIA GPU. On a Mac the checkpoint loads, then the first `decide()` call fails with `NotImplementedError: The operator 'aten::_flash_attention_forward' is not currently implemented for the MPS device`, because the sliding-window layers call `torch.nn.attention.varlen.varlen_attn`, which PyTorch only provides for CUDA. Calling `karpo_apple_silicon.install()` before the first `decide()` replaces that call with banded masked attention. Without CUDA it also lifts a global-layer kernel restriction that otherwise prevents CPU execution. On CPU the real 12B has been run on an Apple Silicon Mac with version 0.2.0 and gave the Apple GPU's answers. `PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=1` does not fix the original error.

## Install and use

```bash
pip install "karpo-decision @ git+https://github.com/machinepulse-ai/karpo-decision@c52d3507a254d3ad8423726c6bc6568c99113e7d"
pip install "karpo-apple-silicon @ git+https://github.com/fluxcodestudio/karpo-apple-silicon"
```

```python
import karpo_apple_silicon
karpo_apple_silicon.install()
from karpo_decision.decider import Decider
decider = Decider.from_pretrained("path/to/karpo-decision-31B", device="mps")
```

## Facts

- Hardware: Apple Silicon Macs (M1, M2, M3, M4 and later), macOS 14 or later. Memory: about 96 GB for the 31B as shipped (62.6 GB of weights), more than 24.0 GB for the 12B. On a 96 GB MacBook Pro (M2 Max) with most other apps closed, version 0.2.0 loaded the 31B and answered requests of up to 10,196 tokens, as shipped and converted to float16; in single runs short requests took seconds (1,049 tokens: 11.9 s in bfloat16, 6.8 s in float16) and long ones minutes (7,464 tokens: 240 s and 159 s), while swap in use grew by about 14 GB.
- Less memory: the MLX path runs the 31B from quantized copies, 34.0 GB at 8 bits and 19.3 GB at 4 bits, text requests only.
- Ready-made MLX weights: https://huggingface.co/jonnyArt/karpo-decision-31B-mlx-8bit and https://huggingface.co/jonnyArt/karpo-decision-31B-mlx-4bit
- Accuracy against MachinePulse's published 31B results (340 requests, 1,606 questions): PyTorch on MPS changed 1 top answer (mean difference 0.0011); version 0.1.0 MLX 8-bit changed 2 (0.0016); version 0.1.0 MLX 4-bit changed 3 of 681 (0.0067). The reworked MLX loader and forward pass (version 0.2.0) have been checked on small random models, and both published folders have the required tensor names and shapes. On the real 4-bit weights version 0.2.0 gave the same top answer as version 0.1.0 on 71 questions (largest probability difference 0.061) with lower peak memory on long requests (23.3 GB to 20.9 GB at 7,464 tokens) and no measurable change in time; on the real 8-bit weights it likewise gave the same top answers on those 71 questions (largest difference 0.040), peaking at 35.6 GB instead of 40.4 GB at 10,196 tokens. On the real 31B in bfloat16, version 0.2.0 gave the same top answers as version 0.1.0 on 31 questions of invented requests (28 of them near-certain; largest probability difference 0.037), and the same top answers as the MLX copies on 71 questions (66 near-certain; largest difference 0.052 for the 8-bit copy and 0.159 for the 4-bit one); converted to float16 it gave the same 71 top answers as in bfloat16 (largest difference 0.028).
- Not covered or not checked: the Qwen-family Karpo models (0.8B to 9B and 27B-act), images, requests longer than 10,196 tokens, comparison with the published results beyond 8,072 tokens or for the 12B (no per-request results are published for it), GGUF / llama.cpp / Ollama. AMD and Intel GPUs have not been checked.
- Port version 0.2.0; tested with karpo-decision 0.1.0 (commits 6600011eb5cf and c52d3507a254, which have the same source files), torch 2.15.0, transformers 5.23.0, mlx 0.32.4, mlx-lm 0.32.2. The installer compares pip's recorded upstream commit because the upstream version has not changed between commits, and checks the attention signature.
